commenti.body:
I'm not sure what you should do. One the one hand, there are things to be understood about his films, and his approach to issues of Christianity are certainly part of that. I don't think I would have appreciated Tarkovsky as much without having read the Bible first. Indeed, some level of familiarity with the Bible is essential for a lot of appreciation of art.

On the other hand, Tarkovsky to me works best as an emotional experience. Knowing certain things can support that experience can can even be essential, but his films in my view are not intellectual exercises that are meant to be worked out. I don't consider myself a cinephile like many on this sub, in that the highly rated films that click with me all have this emphasis on the priority of emotion rather than intellect. I can't stand many of the "interesting" films (looking at Kubrick and the like), but Tarkovsky and the like just do it for me. His approach is very different from Kubrick's and should be experienced differently too.

In the end, you are the best judge. Personally, I would want to know something about Christianity and history before seeing Andrei Rublev, and have some experience with SF before seeing other films of his, but you need to make up your own mind in the end. In any case Tarkovsky films are something to come back to again and again. In my mind, there was no-one to equal him.

Are you watching tarkovsky at only 13 years old?  wow, I don't think I fully understand you and I'm almost 30 years old...

Andrei Rublev may be the one that connected with me the worst, I like his subsequent works more, but keep in mind that it is a slow film that can become tiresome, and it also deals with very complex themes.

Here's a great quote by Tarkovsky:

"Everybody asks me what things mean in my films. This is terrible! An artist doesn’t have to answer for his meanings. I don’t think so deeply about my work—I don’t know what my symbols may represent. What matters to me is that they arouse feelings, any feelings you like, based on whatever your inner response might be. If you look for a meaning, you’ll miss everything that happens. Thinking during a film interferes with your experience of it. Take a watch to pieces, it doesn’t work. Similarly with a work of art, there’s no way it can be analyzed without destroying it."

Just let it wash over you. Also Rublev has a ton of complex historical and religious backdrop, which the rest of his films don't have, so don't worry. I recommend you try Mirror.
